sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Synaptic cleft peroxidase activity detected at excitatory synapses, confirming surface display and proper synaptic localization of the HRP-LRRTM1 fusion; synaptogenic function not separately re-assayed in this study but synaptic cleft residency is preserved.
sites.rationale: LRRTM1 has a signal peptide spanning residues 1–34 (landmarks); the mature extracellular domain begins at residue 35. An N-terminal tag must be placed after the SP cleavage site (after residue 34) to avoid being cleaved off. L3 explicitly describes 'N-terminal, extracellular-facing fusions of HRP' with full-length LRRTM1, and there is exactly one extracellular terminus (the mature N-terminus), so the junction is unambiguously insert_after_residue=34. Python confirmed residue 34 = A and residue 35 = A; the site is 393 residues from the TM boundary, well clear of any constraint. Full-length LRRTM1 was engineered with an N-terminal, extracellular-facing HRP fusion and expressed in neurons; the construct was used as a synaptic cleft peroxidase to biotinylate proteins at excitatory synapses, demonstrating surface display and correct synaptic targeting of the tagged protein.

sources.claim: We therefore generated N-terminal, extracellular-facing fusions of HRP with three known glutamatergic excitatory synaptic cleft-resident proteins (Nlgn1, Lrrtm1, and Lrrtm2 ( Linhoff et al., 2009 ; Song et al., 1999 )) and two known GABAergic inhibitory synaptic cleft resident proteins (Slitrk3 and Nlgn2 ( Chih et al., 2006 ; Takahashi et al., 2012 ; Varoqueaux et al., 2004 )) ( Figure 1C ).

literature_notes: L1 and L2 both describe a C-terminal CFP fusion of full-length LRRTM1 that retains synaptogenic activity. The C-terminus of LRRTM1 is intracellular (residues 449–522 per the authoritative landmarks), so this is not an extracellular surface-tag site; it is recorded in other_positions. L3 grounds the sole surface site: the N-terminal extracellular HRP fusion. No ledger line names an internal extracellular loop insertion for LRRTM1, so no internal sites are proposed.

literature_other_positions.note: CFP fused to the C-terminus of full-length LRRTM1; the C-terminus (residues 449–522) is intracellular per topology landmarks; synaptogenic activity was robustly preserved (L2), making this a validated intracellular tag site but not a surface tag site.
